$comment: Catalogue of questions of the package (DECISION-0190): each card is a parameterised §172 query template with its evidence of execution, the boundaries carry the verbatim limitation from package-info.json. Gate: check_package_questions.py --only <package> --emit.

tasks.title: General provisions of the chapter on validity (art. 3.1.1–3.1.4)
Grounds for avoidance and the effects of avoidance (art. 3.2.1–3.2.17)
Illegality: a contract infringing a mandatory rule (art. 3.3.1, 3.3.2)

questions.question: Is an allowance in money due instead of restitution in kind (art. 3.2.15(2)-(3))?

branches.summary: Article 3.2.15(2). If restitution in kind is not possible or appropriate, an allowance has to be made in money whenever reasonable
Article 3.2.15(2). If restitution in kind is not possible or appropriate, an allowance has to be made in money whenever reasonable

questions.question: Is the effect of avoidance limited to individual terms (art. 3.2.13)?

branches.summary: Article 3.2.13. Where a ground of avoidance affects only individual terms, the effect of avoidance is limited to those terms
Article 3.2.13. Where a ground of avoidance affects only individual terms, the effect of avoidance is limited to those terms

questions.question: Was the notice of avoidance given within a reasonable time (art. 3.2.12)?
Does the avoidance have retroactive effect (art. 3.2.14)?
Does the chapter deal with the incapacity of a party (art. 3.1.1)?
Does the chapter apply to a unilateral communication of intention (art. 3.2.17)?
Has the contract or the term been adapted to reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing (art. 3.2.7(2)-(3))?

branches.summary: Article 3.2.7(3). A court may also adapt the contract or term upon the request of the party receiving notice of avoidance, provided that party informs the other promptly and before reliance
Article 3.2.7(2). Upon the request of the party entitled to avoidance, a court may adapt the contract or term in order to make it accord with reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing

questions.question: Is the contract treated as concluded as the mistaken party understood it (art. 3.2.10(1))?
Has the contract been avoided by notice (art. 3.2.11)?

branches.summary: Article 3.2.11. The right of a party to avoid the contract is exercised by notice to the other party
Article 3.2.11. On notice to the other party the contract is avoided

questions.question: Are the effects of the infringement those prescribed by the mandatory rule itself (art. 3.3.1(1))?
Does an attempt to exclude the mandatory provisions of the chapter have effect (art. 3.1.4)?
Are the expenses of preserving what was received recoverable (art. 3.2.15(4))?
Is the erroneous assumption a mistake (art. 3.2.1, 3.2.3)?

branches.summary: Article 3.2.1. Mistake is an erroneous assumption relating to facts or to law existing when the contract was concluded
Article 3.2.3. An error occurring in the expression or transmission of a declaration is considered to be a mistake of the person from whom the declaration emanated

questions.question: Is a party that knew of the ground for avoidance liable in damages (art. 3.2.16)?
May a party avoid the contract for fraud, threat or gross disparity (art. 3.2.5–3.2.8)?

branches.summary: Article 3.2.5. A party may avoid the contract when it has been led to conclude it by the other party's fraudulent representation or fraudulent non-disclosure
Article 3.2.7(1). A party may avoid the contract if at the time of its conclusion the contract unjustifiably gave the other party an excessive advantage
Article 3.2.6. A party may avoid the contract when it has been led to conclude it by the other party's unjustified threat which is so imminent and serious as to leave no reasonable alternative
Article 3.2.9. If the party entitled to avoid confirms the contract after the period for giving notice has begun to run, avoidance is excluded
Article 3.2.8(1). Where the ground is imputable to a third person for whose acts the other party is responsible, the contract may be avoided under the same conditions
Article 3.2.8(2). Where the ground is imputable to a third person for whose acts the other party is not responsible, the contract may be avoided if that party knew or ought to have known of it

questions.question: May a party avoid the contract for mistake (art. 3.2.2, 3.2.4)?

branches.summary: Article 3.2.2(2)(b). A party may not avoid the contract where the risk of mistake was assumed or should be borne by it

Article 3.2.2(1)(a). A party may avoid the contract for a mistake of decisive importance where the other party made, caused or knew of the mistake and it was contrary to fair dealing to leave the party in error
Article 3.2.2(1)(b). A party may avoid the contract for a mistake of decisive importance where the other party had not at the time of avoidance reasonably acted in reliance on the contract
Article 3.2.2(2)(a). A party may not avoid the contract if it was grossly negligent in committing the mistake
Article 3.2.10(2). Where the right to avoidance is lost, the party may no longer avoid the contract for mistake
Article 3.2.4. A party is not entitled to avoid the contract on the ground of mistake if the circumstances afford, or could have afforded, a remedy for non-performance

questions.question: May a party avoid an individual term of the contract (art. 3.2.7(1))?
May a party claim restitution of what it has supplied (art. 3.2.15(1), 3.3.2(3))?

branches.summary: Article 3.3.2(3). If restitution is granted, the rules set out in Article 3.2.15 apply with appropriate adaptations
Article 3.2.15(1). On avoidance either party may claim restitution of whatever it has supplied, provided that it concurrently makes restitution of whatever it has received

questions.question: From which moment does the time for avoiding an individual term run (art. 3.2.12(2))?
Are the remedies under the contract available where the mandatory rule is silent on the effects (art. 3.3.1(2))?
May restitution be granted under a contract infringing a mandatory rule (art. 3.3.2(1))?
Has the right to avoid been lost (art. 3.2.10(2))?
Is the threat unjustified (art. 3.2.6)?
Does the mere agreement of the parties suffice to conclude, modify or terminate the contract (art. 3.1.2)?
Do initial impossibility and the lack of a right to dispose affect the validity of the contract (art. 3.1.3)?

branches.summary: Article 3.1.3(1). The mere fact that at the time of the conclusion of the contract the performance of the obligation assumed was impossible does not affect the validity of the contract
Article 3.1.3(2). The mere fact that at the time of the conclusion of the contract a party was not entitled to dispose of the assets does not affect the validity of the contract

questions.question: Is the power of the court to adapt the contract or the term active (art. 3.2.7(2))?

branches.summary: Article 3.2.7(2). Upon the request of the party entitled to avoidance, a court may adapt the contract or term in order to make it accord with reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing

questions.question: Is the power of a party to avoid the contract by notice active (art. 3.2.11)?

branches.summary: Article 3.2.11. The right of a party to avoid the contract is exercised by notice to the other party

boundaries.question: Which rule of the applicable law is mandatory and what does it prescribe on infringement?
boundaries.limitation: THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them, or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law; they do not replace the mandatory rules of the applicable law (article 1.4, hub `unidroit.picc`).

boundaries.question: What does the 1980 UN Convention answer on the validity of the contract?
boundaries.limitation: HERE THE CONVENTION IS SILENT BY ITS OWN DECLARATION: article 4(a) takes the validity of the contract and of its provisions out of its subject matter. Chapter 3 of the Principles answers where the Convention declines to, and in substance there is no bridge between them.

boundaries.question: Does the party have capacity and what follows from its incapacity?
boundaries.limitation: THE CHAPTER DOES NOT DEAL WITH CAPACITY (article 3.1.1): the conditions of a party's capacity are a question of the applicable law and an input of the case. The model answers this with a boundary rather than a conclusion.

boundaries.question: Is the mistake material, is the threat imminent and is the advantage excessive?
boundaries.limitation: THE EVALUATIVE ELEMENTS OF CHAPTER 3 GO THROUGH THE §47.3 JUDGMENT CHANNEL with the organ `Tribunal`: whether a reasonable person would have made the mistake material (3.2.2), a departure from reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing (3.2.2), the imminence and gravity of a threat (3.2.6), an excessive and unjustified advantage (3.2.7), a reasonable time for notice (3.2.12), the unreasonableness of upholding the remaining contract (3.2.13), a reasonable allowance in money (3.2.15), the reasonableness of remedies and of restitution in the case of illegality (3.3.1, 3.3.2). The model neither decides them nor substitutes a guess.

boundaries.question: Does the infringed rule prescribe the effects for the contract itself?
boundaries.limitation: WHICH RULE IS MANDATORY AND WHAT IT PRESCRIBES IS AN INPUT OF THE CASE: article 3.3.1 refers to the infringed rule itself, and the Principles step in only where it is silent. Neither the list of such rules nor their effects is carried into the model.

boundaries.question: Which other factors are taken into account in assessing the reasonableness of a remedy?
boundaries.limitation: THE LISTS OF FACTORS IN ARTICLES 3.2.7 AND 3.3.1 ARE NOT EXHAUSTIVE ("among other factors", "in particular"): the seven criteria of article 3.3.1(3) and the two factors of article 3.2.7 are named in the request for a judgment rather than spread into separate premises — otherwise the model would pass off its own completeness as the rule.
